metadata.description: `repomd.json` — the per-index catalog manifest, epoch 1 (PROP-005 §2.4), modelled after RPM's `repomd.xml`. Root type `Repomd`: nine required fields; the `files` map is path-keyed and its values are the tagged union `RepomdFileEntry` (`kind` discriminator, lowercase tags). Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/index/e1/repomd/`.

Path-keyed map of file and directory entries beneath the data directory (excluding `state/`). Keys are POSIX-style relative paths (`primary.jsonl`, `by-name`, …). No `skip_serializing_if` on the writer, so the map is emitted even when empty.

One entry of the manifest's `files` map — a tagged union keyed by `kind`: `directory` carries an entry count, `file` carries size + sha256. Tags are lowercase, per the writer's `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase")]`. Local to this schema: no other schema consumes the manifest's file table.
How many entries the directory holds (files in `by-cap/`, candidate sets in `by-name/`).

File size in bytes, encoded as a canonical decimal string: ASCII digits only, no sign, no leading zeros (except the single digit `0` for zero), value within the unsigned 64-bit range. Integers wider than 32 bits travel as decimal strings by the owner's standing rule (2026-08-20): JTD (RFC 8927) has no 64-bit integer type at all — `uint64` and `int64` are both rejected by the pinned generator as InvalidType (measured 2026-08-15) — so the string form is the only way the schema can describe the writer's `u64` truthfully. Failure mode: a non-numeric or non-canonical string (or a JSON number where the string form is expected) is refused loudly by the consumer at value-parse time; the field's type is never silently loosened (PROP-044 law 1). Until 2026-08-20 this field was `uint32` with the divergence recorded in its description; the wire break is formats/breaks/003.md.
